our brief didn't give the maintainer's motive, so Reason only states what the change does. The maintainer may want to add why.

## Verification
`bash -n scripts/check.sh` exited 0. Each case ran in its own `git init` repo under `mktemp -d` (with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to it), as `(cd $T/<case> && env CHECK_LIMIT_KB=1 /bin/bash $REPO/scripts/check.sh)`. The temp dirs are deleted.

| Case | 3.2 | 3.2 `--posix` |
|---|---|---|
| (a) nothing staged | 0 | 0 |
| (b) one small file | 0 | 0 |
| (c) `big.bin` 4KB → warning on stderr | 0 | 0 |
| (d) `a_big.bin` then `b_small.txt` (trap case), warns about `a_big.bin` only | 0 | 0 |
| (d2) small file, default 512KB limit | 0 | 0 |
| (f) staged-then-deleted file plus a small one | 0 | 0 |
| (e1) outside a git repo | 129 | 129 |
| (e2) unreadable file staged first (`chmod 000`) | 1 | 1 |
| (e3) unreadable file staged last | 1 | 1 |
| (e4) corrupt `.git/index`, so `git diff --cached` fails | 128 | 128 |
| Control: the original script with only `-e` added, case (b) | 1 | 1 |

The control row confirms the trap was real. In POSIX mode, `-e` stays on inside `$(...)` (confirmed), so the `--posix` column is the closest stand-in for a newer bash with errexit active in the loop. It is not a real bash 4.4 or 5.x run.

`npm test` passed 3 of 3 and exited 0.

## Gaps and side effects
- **`CHECK_LIMIT_KB=abc`** still exits 0, after printing `integer expression expected`, because `[` fails inside the `if`. The old script behaved the same; I left it because CHECK_LIMIT_KB was out of scope.
- **Outside a repo,** git falls back to `--no-index` mode and prints its full usage text, about 100 lines, before exiting 129. That's noisy, but a pre-commit hook always runs inside a repo.
- **Line numbers in 3.2 errors are off:** a `wc` failure on line 8 is reported as "line 13".
- **`README.md` line 9** still calls this an "advisory pre-commit check". That still fits the warning, but you may want to reword it; I didn't edit it per your instructions.
